cells.tense: Right now the feeling has come to rest, and you are sitting with what it already knows.
cells.act: read the hardest page of it twice, slowly, before you stop
cells.ask: Pick the hard thing you keep circling about someone close, and give it fifteen quiet minutes before you decide anything. Read it twice, slow, then stop.
cells.core:
When you're feeling with someone, the feeling comes in and rests a while before it turns into anything — nothing pushed out past where it actually is, nothing rehearsed for the other person's benefit. On the good days, you can sit beside what someone is carrying without needing to move it, fix it, or add your own part, and the connection keeps its shape without you holding it up.

What you're free to feed next is depth — going all the way into a pattern until you meet its edge. Try it on the hard thing, not the easy one. Read the hardest page of it twice, slowly, before you stop. Fifteen minutes is enough. You'll know the edge when you feel it, and you'll come back still inside the connection instead of outside it.
cells.sheetLine: Take the hard thing and read it twice before you move.
cells.verb: Settling into what you already feel
cells.place: In the company of someone close you are feeling alongside

cells.tense: You are bracing for a closeness that has not happened yet, and the waiting is wearing you down.
cells.act: count what the ending gave you
cells.ask: Name one closeness that ended — a stretch of time with someone, a way you two were. This week, count what it gave you: what it grew, what it cost, what's still yours.
cells.core:
The feeling is there and the person is mostly there too, but you've started lining up how this could go before it happens, and what reaches the other person first is the managing, not the warmth. When it's going well, this kind of bond honors difference and doesn't need to fuse — two people stay two people, neither one swallowed. Braced, you're arranging a connection that hasn't started yet.

Under that sits a change that hasn't finished being honored. So before the next thing begins, count what the last one yielded: what it grew in you, what it cost, what's still yours from it. Walk while you do it, or sit with a page. Gathering what the ending grew is the whole act. New ground reads differently once you've taken in what the last ground gave.
cells.sheetLine: What ended already paid you something. Add it up.

cells.tense: You are still standing at a door that closed behind you, feeling the old shape of it.
cells.act: bring the two sides of your thinking into one plan
cells.ask: Choose one relationship you care about and haven't been showing up for. Set what you think about it beside what it stirs in you, then gather both into one small plan — a note you'll send, a walk you'll propose. Nothing after it.
cells.core:
Where people should be meeting, there's a distance that hasn't lifted. Someone says something warm and it lands as a thin signal; you wait for something back and it doesn't arrive, so you answer carefully instead. You know the connection matters. You just aren't in it. It's been this way a while, and the shape of it is familiar.

This isn't a feeling problem — it's scattered thinking under the feeling. Pick one relationship you care about and haven't been showing up for. One, not the whole web. Set what you think about it beside what it stirs in you, in the same place, then gather both sides into one small plan. A note you'll send, a walk you'll propose, a question you'll ask. Small and real. The thinking is what restarts the meeting.
cells.sheetLine: Set both sides down together, and make one small plan.

cells.tense: The stillness is there in you already, and your name for it is being an easy person to be around.
cells.act: stay in the depth of it instead of surfacing
cells.ask: For the next few weeks, when something honest passes between you and someone close and you catch yourself moving past it, stay in it one breath longer. Keep doing that, without announcing it.
cells.core:
There's a way you sit with what someone close is carrying — quiet, unhurried, no advice coming. You'd probably describe yourself as easy to be around, or just as someone who listens. That listening is doing real work in the connection, and the description leaves the worker out of it.

It rests on a plain fact: when something honest passes between two people, most of the time it gets stepped over, and you do it too. Next time it happens — the honesty moving past you toward whatever's next — stay in it one breath longer before you go. Nothing announced, nothing added. Just stay. That's the same move a mind makes when it goes all the way into a thing instead of surfacing up, and here it's the whole of the meeting.
cells.sheetLine: When something real passes through, stay one breath longer.
